problem.title_as_question: How does string bed tension/stiffness expose swing speed mismatches and cause shots to spray?
problem.definition: When playing with a string bed that is too soft for your swing speed, oblique brushing racket head speed increases vertical launch just as much as topspin, causing well-struck balls to launch too deep and spraying, which leads the nervous system to subconsciously brake the swing.
prerequisites: Players taking full-speed swings with an oblique brushing path attempting to generate heavy topspin margin.

symptoms.description: Centered, well-struck topspin shots launch unexpectedly deep or fly long past the baseline despite aggressive brushing.
Off-center hits and shanks surprisingly carry deep rather than dying short near the service line.
The player leaks kinetic energy right before impact as the nervous system adds subtle brakes and stoppages to the stroke.
Sensory confusion where clean mechanics produce spraying long, leading the player to feel helpless and mistrust their stroke.

causes.statement: At higher swing speeds on a soft string bed, the ball sinks deep into the pocket and is flung along the swing path rather than deflecting cleanly off the face angle.
Increasing tangential/brushing racket head speed on soft strings creates unwanted vertical exit launch angle simultaneously with topspin.
Swinging faster than the playable threshold of a soft or lost-tension string bed.

solutions.summary: Intentionally swing 20% slower with the exact same mechanics to see if the balls immediately land consistently inside the court with predictable depth.
solutions.external_goal: Place consecutive topspin rally balls safely several feet inside the baseline without spraying.

solutions.summary: Increase string tension or switch to a stiffer string setup that can physically support fast, oblique swing speeds without excess vertical launch.
